title: First-in-human study of ATX-898 as monotherapy and in combination with other anti-neoplastic agents, in participants with advanced solid tumors
official: First-in-human study of ATX-898 as monotherapy and in combination with other anti-neoplastic agents, in participants with advanced solid tumors

interventions.name: Fulvestrant Hikma 250 mg/5ml solução injetável em seringa pré-cheia

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Has histologically or cytologically confirmed advanced solid tumor malignancy that is metastatic or locally advanced and unresectable
2. Male participant (with a successful vasectomy) and his female partner(s) who are of childbearing potential must agree to consistently use 1 barrier method (e.g., condom with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository) starting at Screening and continuing throughout the study period and for at least 90 days after the last dose of ATX-898 for monotherapy treatment and at least 2 years after the last dose of fulvestrant for fulvestrant combination treatment.
3. Has adequate organ function as defined by the protocol
4. Male participant with a pregnant partner must consistently use a condom to prevent potential fetal exposure.
5. Participant, or legally authorized representative if applicable, is capable of understanding the written ICF and other patient-facing study materials, provides signed and witnessed written informed consent, and agrees to comply with protocol requirements.
6. [Part 1A] Has received one or more standard systemic therapies and additional standard systemic therapies are either not available, contraindicated, or the participant is deemed by the Investigator to not be an appropriate candidate for available standard therapy option(s)
7. [Part 1A] For participants with solid tumors other than breast cancer, has protocol required biomarker positive status. For participants with HR+/HER2- breast cancer, must have HR+/HER2–, HR+/HERlow (as defined by a HER2 IHC score of 1+ or by a score of 2+ with a negative FISH determined in a CLIA-certified or locally equivalent clinical laboratory), or HR+/HERultralow (as defined by HER2 IHC 0 with membrane staining determined in a CLIA-certified or locally equivalent clinical laboratory).
8. Is ≥18 years of age at the time of signing the informed consent form (ICF)
9. Has ECOG performance status score of 0 or 1
10. Must consent to a pre-treatment tumor biopsy (collected during screening) or have available archival tumor tissue in the past 5 years. On-treatment biopsies are optional.
11. Before study entry, a female must meet one of the following, or according to local regulations: a) be of nonchildbearing potential, defined as per protocol; b) Be a female of childbearing potential (FCBP; any female participant who does not meet the nonchildbearing criteria above) who agrees to remain on 1 highly effective method and 1 additional effective (barrier) method of contraception from initiation of study treatment, throughout the study and for at least 6 months after the last dose of ATX-898 for monotherapy treatment. For combination treatment, the participant must agree to use 1 highly effective method and 1 additional effective barrier method (e.g., condom with spermicidal foam/gel/film/cream/suppository) of contraception throughout the study for at least 2 years after the last dose of fulvestrant for fulvestrant combination treatment or at least 6 months after the last dose of ATX-898 if fulvestrant has not been part of the combination treatment.
12. [Part 1B] Has protocol required biomarker positive status.
13. A female participant must agree to refrain from donating eggs (ova, oocytes) for the purpose of assisted reproduction from initiation, during the study and for a period of at least 6 months after the last dose of ATX-898 for monotherapy treatment and at least 2 years after the last dose of fulvestrant for fulvestrant combination treatment.
14. A FCBP must have a negative, highly sensitive serum (β-human chorionic gonadotropin) pregnancy test at Screening.
15. Female participants must agree not to breastfeed starting at Screening, throughout the study period, and for at least 6 months after the last dose of ATX-898 for monotherapy treatment and at least 2 years after the last dose of fulvestrant for fulvestrant combination treatment.
16. [Part 1A] For participants with HR+/HER2- breast cancer, participants must have received prior systemic therapy - can be in the adjuvant or metastatic setting
17. [Part 1A] For backfill cohorts: must have at least 1 measurable lesion per RECIST 1.1. Note: Previously irradiated lesion may only be counted as a target lesion if there is clear progression since the irradiation.
18. Male participant (without vasectomy) whose female partner(s) is/are of childbearing potential must agree to do the following: a) Use 2 forms of contraception consistently (at least 1 of which must be a barrier method [e.g., condom with spermicidal foam/gel/film/ cream/suppository], and the other of which must be a highly effective method of contraception) starting at Screening and continuing throughout the study period and for at least 90 days after the last dose of ATX-898 for monotherapy treatment and at least 2 years after the last dose of fulvestrant for fulvestrant combination treatment. b) Refrain from donating sperm from Day 1 until at least 90 days after the final administration of ATX-898 and at least 2 years after the last dose of fulvestrant for fulvestrant combination treatment.
19. [Part 1B] Cohort B2 and B3 only: Must have received systemic therapy
20. [Part 1B] Cohort B2 only: Has recurrent or metastatic cancer
21. [Part 1B] Cohort B3 only: Has an advanced or refractory solid tumor malignancy of a cancer type not included in other inclusion criteria
22. [Part 1B] Must have at least 1 measurable lesion per RECIST 1.1 Note: Previously irradiated lesion may only be counted as a target lesion if there is clear progression since the irradiation.
23. [Part 2A] Has received systemic treatment for stage III (locally advanced), unresectable locoregional disease, or stage IV disease.
24. [Part 2B] Has received systemic treatment for stage III (locally advanced), unresectable locoregional disease, or stage IV disease.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Has had prior organ transplantation.
2. Has a history of or a suspected allergy or hypersensitivity to ATX-898, other study treatments, or their excipients; hypersensitivity to peanut (ribociclib cohorts only).
3. Has any condition requiring systemic corticosteroids (daily prednisone equivalent doses not exceeding a total dose of 140 mg over the past 14 days) or other immunosuppressive therapy within 2 weeks prior to the start of study treatment. Note: Inhaled, intranasal, intra-articular, or topical steroids are permitted. Transient short-term use of systemic corticosteroids for transient conditions (e.g., allergic conditions, asthma/chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) exacerbations, contrast allergy) is permitted.
4. Has known, uncontrolled human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-1 infection or acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS), with the following exceptions: • Participants with known HIV infection are permitted if they have controlled infection (undetectable viral load [HIV ribonucleic acid (RNA) polymerase chain reaction (PCR)] and CD4 count ≥350 cells/μL either spontaneously or on a stable antiviral regimen). For participants with controlled HIV infection, monitoring will be performed per local standards. • Participants with AIDS who have not experienced an opportunistic infection in the past 12 months may be eligible with Medical Monitor approval.
5. Has positive hepatitis B surface antigen or hepatitis C virus (HCV) antibody (anti-HCV) test, clinically active or chronic liver diseases, including liver cirrhosis of Child-Pugh Class C. Note: Participants with treated hepatitis B or C and positive antibody test are eligible only if followed by a negative RNA test (i.e., viral load below the limit of quantification or on a stable antiviral regimen).
6. Has uncontrolled intercurrent illness including, but not limited to, ongoing or active infection, symptomatic congestive heart failure, unstable angina pectoris, cardiac arrythmia, or psychiatric illness/social situation that would limit compliance with study requirements. Note: Participants with a history of myocardial infarction, unstable angina, or acute coronary syndrome within the 6 months prior to enrollment are excluded.
7. Has any condition for which, in the opinion of the Investigator, participation would not be in the best interest of the participant or would prevent, limit, or confound the protocol-specified assessments (for example, interstitial lung disease, severe dyspnea at rest or requiring oxygen therapy, severe renal impairment, history of major surgical resection involving the stomach or small bowel, or preexisting Crohn’s disease or ulcerative colitis or a preexisting chronic condition resulting in baseline Grade 2 or higher diarrhea).
8. For abemaciclib cohorts only: The patient has a personal history of any of the following conditions: syncope of cardiovascular etiology, ventricular arrhythmia of pathological origin (including, but not limited to, ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation), or sudden cardiac arrest.
9. For ribociclib cohorts only: History of pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease.
10. Has received prior treatment with treatment directed at the protocol defined target.
11. Has any of the protocol defined mutations or copy number loss.
12. For ribociclib cohorts only: Participant currently receiving any of the following substances and cannot discontinue them 7 days prior to Cycle 1 Day 1 (C1D1): • Concomitant medication(s) with a known risk to prolong the QT interval and/or known to cause Torsades de Pointes (TdP) that cannot be discontinued or replaced by safe alternative mediation (e.g., within 5 half-lives or 7 days before starting study drug) are not permitted • Concomitant medications, herbal supplements, and/or fruits (e.g., grapefruit, pummelos, star fruit, Seville oranges) and their juices that are strong inducers or inhibitors of cytochrome P450 3A4/5 (CYP3A4/5) • Medications that have a narrow therapeutic window and are predominantly metabolized through CYP3A4/5
13. Is unable to swallow tablets or has malabsorption syndrome, disease significantly affecting gastrointestinal function, resection of the stomach or small bowel, symptomatic inflammatory bowel disease or ulcerative colitis, or partial or complete bowel obstruction
14. Has history (within ≤2 years before screening) of a solid tumor or hematological malignancy that is histologically distinct from the cancers being studied Note: Exceptions include cervical carcinoma in situ, superficial noninvasive bladder tumors, curatively treated nonmelanoma skin cancer, or any malignancy that in the opinion of the Investigator, with concurrence with the Sponsor's medical monitor, is considered cured with minimal risk.
15. Has symptomatic CNS metastases at screening or asymptomatic central nervous system (CNS) metastases requiring corticosteroids to control symptoms within 28 days prior to the first dose of ATX-898 Note: Known CNS metastases are allowed if they have been previously treated with surgery and/or radiotherapy with no evidence of radiographic progression or hemorrhage within 28 days before the start of study treatment, are asymptomatic, and do not require treatment with corticosteroids to control symptoms.
16. Treatment with any local or systemic antineoplastic therapy or investigational anticancer agent within the following time periods prior to initiation of study treatment: • For ATX-898 monotherapy: 14 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, up to a maximum washout period of 28 days • For ATX-898, fulvestrant, and abemaciclib combination therapy: 21 days • For ATX-898, fulvestrant, and ribociclib combination therapy: 14 days or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, up to a maximum washout period of 28 days.
17. Radiotherapy within 14 days before the initiation of study treatment Note: Palliative radiotherapy for pain can be administered at any time before the first dose of study treatment.
18. Has toxicities from previous anticancer therapies that have not resolved to baseline levels or to CTCAE Grade ≤1, with the exception of alopecia any grade and Grade ≤2 peripheral neuropathy.
19. Has had major surgery (e.g., requiring general anesthesia) within 21 days before the initiation of study treatment, will not have fully recovered from prior surgery, or has surgery planned during the time in which the participant is expected to participate in the study Note: Participants with planned surgical procedures to be conducted under local anesthesia may participate in the study.
